programme: A differentiation-versus-proliferation switch built around retinoid and AP-2/KLF epithelial-identity signaling (RARG, TFAP2C, KLF5) opposed by an ID1/MBD2-CHD4 repression arm that blocks terminal differentiation: ID1 sequesters differentiation-driving bHLH/Smad activity while MBD2 and CHD4 (the two literal components of the MBD2-NuRD corepressor complex) silence differentiation genes at chromatin. E2F5 supplies the cell-cycle output of that block, NFE2L2 buffers the oxidative load of sustained proliferation, STAT5A carries cytokine/growth-factor input into the same state, PRRX1 marks the mesenchymal/stromal compartment that reinforces it, and PER2 sits as a circadian brake directly upstream of the EMT effector genes this network would otherwise switch on: PER2's own target list here is SNAI2, TWIST1, and SERPINE1, the same genes TFAP2C/KLF5/ID1/PRRX1 activity converges on.
role_in_a: In lung cancer this is the documented EMT/dedifferentiation and therapy-resistance engine: KLF5 and PRRX1 drive EMT and CAF-mediated immune suppression (41074131, 39010054), TFAP2C activates resistance and progression programs (40777819, 39716275), ID1 promotes metastasis via TAM and senescent-endothelium signaling (41857107, 42172707), MBD2 is stabilized to drive MAPK-dependent progression while CHD4 supports DNA-damage response and treatment resistance (42401357, 41930570, 40004553), NFE2L2 sustains an oxidative-stress-adapted, drug-resistant state (42255480), STAT5A and E2F5 feed proliferative/survival signaling (42315836, 34634227 — the latter carries a published Expression of Concern), and PER2 loss removes the circadian brake on tumor growth (41736190, 42186698).
role_in_b: In psoriasis the same module would be expected to run the opposite clinical phenotype of the differentiation block: instead of invasive dedifferentiation, a stalled proliferation/differentiation switch in keratinocytes that produces hyperproliferative, incompletely differentiated epidermis, with PER2 loss removing the circadian check on the SNAI2/TWIST1/SERPINE1-type effector genes and worsening IL-17-driven disease, as shown directly for PER2 (41864430). None of the other ten carrying factors have any retrieved psoriasis evidence to confirm this role.
shared_axis: Both diseases feature a proliferating, stratified/glandular epithelium in which retinoid- and AP-2/KLF-driven differentiation cues are opposed by an ID1/NuRD repression arm and gated by the circadian clock; lung cancer pushes this axis toward invasive dedifferentiation (EMT) while psoriasis would push the same axis toward blocked terminal differentiation with hyperproliferation, so the same regulators could plausibly run divergent tissue-appropriate versions of one differentiation-control circuit.
reasoning: The module is concretely nameable from the given target lists alone (KRT14 under TFAP2C, SNAI2/TWIST1/SERPINE1 under PER2, PPARG-adjacent differentiation logic) and the record independently anchors nearly every carrying factor in lung cancer with multiple specific PMIDs, which is what 'strong' requires. But the record explicitly states no factor besides PER2 has any psoriasis evidence, and PER2's single psoriasis paper uses a mouse psoriasiform-dermatitis model found only via an alternative search term — so the cross-disease link is my inference from the programme's logic, not something documented, which is exactly what 'unexpected' describes rather than 'supported' or 'established'.
support: 41074131 (KLF5 drives EMT/metastasis in lung adenocarcinoma); 39010054 (PRRX1-OLR1 CAF axis in lung cancer); 40777819 and 39716275 (TFAP2C drives resistance/progression in lung cancer); 41857107 and 42172707 (ID1 promotes lung cancer metastasis via TAM/endothelial signaling); 42401357 (MBD2 stabilized, drives NSCLC progression via MAPK); 41930570 and 40004553 (CHD4 in tumor progression/DNA damage response, reviews); 42255480 (NRF2/NFE2L2 addiction in cancer); 42315836 (STAT5A in an axis suppressing SCLC via PARP1); 34634227 (E2F5 in NSCLC via circRNA — carries a published Expression of Concern, weak citation); 41736190 and 42186698 (PER2/circadian clock in lung cancer and lung disease context); 41864430 (Per2 deficiency worsens IL-17-driven psoriasiform dermatitis — the only psoriasis-side evidence, and via an alternative disease term).
how_to_falsify: In matched lesional vs. non-lesional psoriatic keratinocytes, profile RARG, KLF5, TFAP2C, ID1, MBD2/CHD4 occupancy and expression, and ask whether they co-occupy the same targets implicated here (e.g. KRT14, and the PER2-repressed SNAI2/TWIST1/SERPINE1 set); then test PER2 knockdown/knockout in human keratinocytes for de-repression of SNAI2/TWIST1/SERPINE1 as seen in the mouse dermatitis model. If expression or occupancy of the non-PER2 factors is absent or unchanged in psoriatic skin, or PER2 loss does not de-repress those same genes in keratinocytes, the shared-axis claim is falsified.
caveats: Tissue pairing is lung epithelium vs. skin epithelium — anatomically distinct, and the 224 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so they are not 224 independent replications; the strongest factors (RARG, KLF5) are concordant in only 112/224 (50%) of comparisons and the weakest carrying factors near 81-83/224 (~36%), well short of near-unanimous support. The single-view exclusions (KDM5D, HMGA2, KLF8, etc.) show the surviving list isn't a one-subgroup artifact, but that only defends recurrence within lung-cancer data, not the psoriasis link. No tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair. One supporting citation (34634227, E2F5) carries a published Expression of Concern and should be weighted down. The psoriasis-side evidence is a single mouse psoriasiform-dermatitis paper (PER2) surfaced only via an alternative search term — the record explicitly notes no genuine joint mechanism was retrieved for any factor.
